item.title: Re: The Shield that Redirects its Damage
item.content:encoded:
PM request acknowledged, time for a followup! :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: An Indian shield from the 16th century that has connection to the 3 main Hindu gods. When held by a living person with the belief of doing heroic deeds will cause a blue energy field to cover it and tempt them to do said heroic deeds. The energy field can redirect any damage that is inflicted upon it right back at the attacker (Examples: Shooting it with a gun will result in bullet wounds appearing in you or slashing at it with a sharp weapon will give you stab wounds and cuts). If its wielder has villainous or wrongful ideas then the shield will be corrupted and its energy field will turn red, fueling its wielder's ideas.

Overall, I don't have much of an issue with the concept, you seem to have a strong grasp on what the skip is. My only main issue with the concept is the the skips overall purpose, as it doesn't seem to be expanded upon much. which in turn makes the concept feel a bit flat.

The current focus: "if you're good then the shield will be blue, and you do good things. And if you're bad the shield will be red, and you do bad things", is a bit of cliche as it feels like it's just making the wearer a super hero or super villain without bringing anything new in.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The shield came to the foundation's attention when reports of a man wielding a glowing blue shield was committing vigilantism in India. An investigation was initiated as several agents were sent to recover it. They were able to subdue the vigilante, but once they removed the shield his body crumbled to dust only leaving behind his equipment and some notes. In the process of being taken to the Foundation it ended up causing some trouble along the way as it switched between blue and red when held by different personnel, causing suspicion and conflict among them. Once finally contained, tests are conducted on the shield and the notes are analyzed to learn more about it.

I quiet liked where the story was going with the suspicion between personnel, but that avenue just sort of stopped abruptly in favour of testing the skip, which made the payoff feel anticlimactic.- what came of the suspicions? who were these characters? what interventions did they have? whats everything building up to?

Along with this, I feel the setup could be stronger as currently the original wearer just sort of feels like a plot device for the Foundation, as he doesn't really contribute much to the narrative, or give any sort of insight into the skip. Rather, he just disappears with no context or development, which feels like a quick way to get out of writing character interactions, especially since the "crumbling into dust" isn't mentioned before or after this.- why does this happen? does the Foundation ever get an any context to this? do they research it? why isn't it mentioned again? what did the "vigilante" actually do?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

-I would recommend focusing your narrative more around the suspicions between characters, and the shields way of showing "good" and "bad".

Also, try to keep away from just turning the wearer's into super heroes (or villains) as it makes the concept feel cliched and hard to get invested in, as characters are much more complex than just "good" or "bad", what where the characters intentions? who were they? why should I as reader care about them? what is considered "good" and "bad" ect.

If you would like any additional feedback, feel welcome to send me a PM :) I look forward to any further edits! and if you're looking for any new perspectives or other critters in general, I would highly recommend the butterfly squad.

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Re: The Shield that Redirects its Damage
item.content:encoded:
Hello HelloThere! let's take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A viking shield that when held by a living person will cause a blue energy field to cover it. The energy field can redirect any damage that is inflicted upon it right back at the attacker (Examples: Shooting it with a gun will result in bullet wounds appearing in you or slashing at it with a sharp weapon will give you stab wounds and cuts). However, it does have its limits.

Overall, the skip feels like a "thing that does a thing", as the object doesn't seem to have much of purpose or origin. The main focus from both the narrative and concept seem to be the effects, which currently fall fairly flat, as there isn't anything beyond "shield that deflects attacks". What about this will make me as the reader invested? is there any sort of history behind the skip? whats its purpose? how do its effects relate to that purpose?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: The shield was discovered in Norway in a viking ship burial by some archaeologists. The SCP came to the foundation's attention when reports of a cursed and powerful shield erupted upon its discovery so an investigation was initiated and the SCP was recovered. Tests and experiments were conducted to understand how it works which usually consisted of D-Class personnel and weaponized machinery attacking it.

While there is a setup here, a strong middle act and payoff are missing. The story isn't building up to anything, or showing much other than "Foundation finds and then tests something". The tests alone won't be able to carry the story, as they don't offer anything to really get invested in.

Along with this the narrative is missing a conflict. All of the events go off without a hitch and the Foundation doesn't have any sort of reason of care about the skip, which makes the story feel a bit flat and unnatural.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is unknown where the shield gained its anomalous ability and who the creator/original wielder was. There is also little information on how the SCP generates its blue energy field though it is possible that there is some sort of mystical or magical force surrounding it.

This feels like a quick/lazy way to explain the skips effects and origin, especially with the lack of other main focuses (the Foundation is only testing the skips effects) in the narrative or concept.

The shield could provide potential use to the foundation, but if fallen into the wrong hands it could lead to many problems.

I would recommend you look at making this more apparent in the narrative (from what I can see this barely gets mention in the story). Show how this would be useful, why it's dangerous in the wrong hands, what would happen ect.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

Recommendations:
-My main issue is the lack of a strong conflict and payoff in the narrative, there isn't much to really get invested in. - I would recommend expanding upon possible ideas for conflict or exploitation. (the Foundation using it for their own gain, other parties trying to steal it, ect.)

-the skip itself only really shows its effects, which alone aren't interesting enough to carry the article. - I wold recommend you get a rough idea of the origin and purpose of the skip, as developing it fully, will allow you to pick and choose what is and isn't necessary to include. (it can also help with developing the narrative!)

- the plot line feels unfinished due to the lack of a strong payoff. - Show something more than just tests, what does everything build up to? why are they testing it? what is learnt by the end? ect.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED

When held by a living person with the belief of doing heroic deeds will cause a blue energy field to cover it and tempt them to do said heroic deeds. The energy field can redirect any damage that is inflicted upon it right back at the attacker (Examples: Shooting it with a gun will result in bullet wounds appearing in you or slashing at it with a sharp weapon will give you stab wounds and cuts). If its wielder has villainous or wrongful ideas then the shield will be corrupted and its energy field will turn red, fueling its wielder's ideas.

Central Narrative: The shield came to the foundation's attention when reports of a man wielding a glowing blue shield was committing vigilantism in India. An investigation was initiated as several agents were sent to recover it. They were able to subdue the vigilante, but once they removed the shield his body crumbled to dust only leaving behind his equipment and some notes. In the process of being taken to the Foundation it ended up causing some trouble along the way as it switched between blue and red when held by different personnel, causing suspicion and conflict among them. Once finally contained, tests are conducted on the shield and the notes are analyzed to learn more about it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There is little information of how the shield was created since the vigilante has been dusted away. However, from his notes and secret text on the shield it is suggested that the object has been passed down by many since the 16th century as well as hints of the 3 major deities of Hindu Mythology having a part in this. The shield could also provide potential use to the foundation (Example: Protection against or recontaining SCPs), but if fallen into the wrong hands (Like the Chaos Insurgency) its power to redirect attacks and fuel people's ideas can cause many problems.

Additional Notes: This is one of the first ideas I came up with. Also, I changed some of it thanks to some recommendations.
